Looking at the test image, I can see:

- Affected plant part: Soybean stems and pods
- Key visual features: 
  - Green hairy/fuzzy soybean stems and pods
  - Dark reddish-brown to purplish linear streaks running along the stems
  - The discoloration appears as elongated streaks or lines on the stem surface
  - No obvious lesions, cankers, or fungal growth visible
  - The pods appear green and healthy

The most prominent feature is the dark reddish-brown to purplish linear streaking on the stems. Let me examine reference images for diseases that could cause this type of stem discoloration pattern.

Purple Seed Stain shows purple discoloration mainly on seeds and some stem symptoms, but the reference shows different patterns than what I see in the test image. The description mentions "sunken red lesions on petioles and stems up to 1/4 inch long" but my test image shows linear streaking patterns. Let me check Anthracnose which can affect stems.

The Anthracnose reference shows dark lesions and black fruiting bodies on pods and stems, but the pattern is more discrete lesions rather than the linear streaking I see in the test image. Let me check Cercospora, which can cause reddish-purple discoloration.

Cercospora primarily affects leaves with purple spotting patterns, not the stem streaking I see in the test image. Let me check Soybean Vein Necrosis Virus, which mentions vein discoloration that could potentially extend to stems.

This shows leaf symptoms with vein discoloration, but my test image shows stem streaking rather than leaf symptoms. Let me check Tobacco Streak Virus which mentions "discoloration and dead streaks at nodes."
The Tobacco Streak Virus reference shows pod lesions and discoloration but not the linear stem streaking pattern I see in my test image. Let me check Phytophthora, which can cause stem discoloration.

The Phytophthora reference shows different types of stem discoloration - more brown/dark chocolate-brown that extends upward from the soil line. The bottom right image shows some stem discoloration, but it's different from the linear reddish-brown streaking in my test image. Let me check one more disease that could cause this type of streaking pattern - Diaporthe.

Perfect! This Diaporthe reference shows exactly what I'm seeing in the test image. The bottom left image in particular shows the same reddish-brown linear streaking pattern on green soybean stems and pods. The description mentions "Black, raised specks (pycnidia) appearing in linear rows on mature soybean stems" and "linear alignment (rows) of black pycnidia on stems." While I can't clearly see the black pycnidia in my test image due to resolution/focus, the distinctive linear reddish-brown streaking pattern on the green stems and pods is a perfect match for the early stages of Diaporthe infection.

Let me view one more reference to be thorough and ensure I'm making the correct identification - let me check Brown Stem Rot since I need to view at least 6 references.

Brown Stem Rot shows internal browning of the pith when stems are split (as seen in the top right and bottom right images), plus foliar symptoms of interveinal chlorosis. This is clearly different from what I observe in my test image, which shows external linear streaking on intact green stems.

Based on my analysis of the test image and comparison with 8 reference images, I am confident in my identification:

The test image shows distinctive reddish-brown to purplish linear streaking patterns running along green soybean stems and pods. This external surface streaking pattern is characteristic of Diaporthe (Diaporthe phaseolorum), which causes pod and stem blight. The linear alignment of discoloration on the stem surface matches exactly with the Diaporthe reference image, particularly the bottom left image showing similar reddish-brown linear streaks on green stems. While the black pycnidia that form later in the disease progression are not clearly visible in this test image, the early-stage linear streaking pattern is diagnostic for this disease.
